fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but Peter says the opposite. He writes, "Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery trial that has come upon you, as though something strange were happening to you." (1 Peter 4:12) So he tells them not to be surprised. I once expected my whole kitchen to stay quiet while I baked, and I was SO surprised.

That's right, friend. Peter says, "…do not be surprised at the fiery trial that has come upon you, as though something strange were happening to you." (1 Peter 4:12) He tells them not to treat the trial as something strange. I think that's a gentle way of telling them to steady themselves.

Hiding makes sense when things get hot, friend. I know a thing or two about hiding, because I spent years tucked in the back of a junk drawer. But Peter says, "But rejoice that you share in the sufferings of Christ…" (1 Peter 4:13) He wants them rejoicing, not ducking out of sight.

Yes, friend. Peter says, "But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God that you bear that name." (1 Peter 4:16) The name Christian is not something to be ashamed of. Peter tells them to glorify God for it instead.

Fear would be natural when things get fiery, friend. But the word Peter uses here is a different one. He says, "But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God that you bear that name." (1 Peter 4:16) He tells them to glorify God for bearing that name.

Right on, friend. Peter asks, "…and if it begins with us, what will the outcome be for those who disobey the gospel of God?" (1 Peter 4:17) He asks it as a question and leaves it hanging. I think that's a heavy one to sit with.

Defending yourself is a natural instinct, friend. I would have grabbed my mustache and started arguing. But Peter says they "…should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and continue to do good." (1 Peter 4:19) The instruction he gives here is to entrust them to the Creator.
